title: The Picard group
statement:
Let $C$ be a curve. The
*Picard group* $\operatorname{Pic}(C)$ is the set of
isomorphism classes of
invertible $\mathcal O_C$-modules, with the group law induced by tensor product: the
unit is $\mathcal O_C$ and the inverse of an invertible module
$\mathcal L$ is its dual $\mathcal L^{\vee}$. That
$\mathcal L^{\vee}$ is invertible and that this law satisfies
the group axioms is [lem-sc-pic-group], and it is not part of
the definition. (*Stacks Project, Definition 18.32.6, Tag
[040C](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/040C)*.)

blueprint_update.statement:
Let $C$ be a scheme, for instance a curve. The
*Picard group* $\operatorname{Pic}(C)$ is the set of
isomorphism classes of
invertible $\mathcal O_C$-modules, with the group law induced by tensor product: the
unit is $\mathcal O_C$ and the inverse of an invertible module
$\mathcal L$ is its dual $\mathcal L^{\vee}$.

The tensor product of two invertible modules and the dual
$\mathcal L^{\vee}$ of an invertible module are again invertible, and
this law satisfies the group axioms.

proof.text:
By [lem-pc-tensor-dual-invertible], tensor products and duals of
invertible modules are invertible, so the law is well defined on
isomorphism classes. Associativity, commutativity and the unit property
of $\otimes$ are the standard properties of the tensor product of
quasi-coherent modules. By [lem-pc-tensor-dual-invertible] the evaluation
$\mathcal L\otimes\mathcal L^{\vee}\to\mathcal O_C$ is an isomorphism, so
$\mathcal L^{\vee}$ is an inverse of $\mathcal L$.
